stories.title: ADAMTS7 impairs endothelial angiogenic function via suppressing POSTN-mediated VEGFR2 activation in pre-eclampsia
stories.description: Angiogenic imbalance-induced endothelial dysfunction is central to pre-eclampsia (PE) pathogenesis. A disintegrin and metalloprotease with thrombospondin motif, member 7 (ADAMTS7) is upregulated in PE placentas and suppresses trophoblast function; however, its role in systemic endothelial dysfunction during PE remains unclear. Here we show a higher placental secretion and plasma level of ADAMTS7 in PE patients. ADAMTS7 circulating levels are positively correlated with systolic and diastolic blood pressure of pregnant women. Besides, hypoxia stimulates ADAMTS7 expression in human trophoblast and vascular cells by a HIF1α-dependent way. Pregnant rats with ADAMTS7 overexpression by adenovirus injection exhibits PE-like symptoms and impaired placental development. Functionally, ADAMTS7 significantly inhibits endothelial angiogenic activity and suppresses vessel formation as evidenced by proliferation, migration, angiogenic assays. Mechanistically, ADAMTS7 binds to and decreases periostin (POSTN), reducing VEGFR2 expression and phosphorylation. This study identifies ADAMTS7 as a pathogenic factor in PE that impaired endothelial angiogenic function, suggesting that targeting ADAMTS7/POSTN/VEGFR2 axis may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for PE. Angiogenic imbalance drives endothelial dysfunction in pre-eclampsia (PE). Here, the authors show the metalloprotease ADAMTS7 is elevated in the circulation of PE patients and impairs endothelial angiogenic function, suggesting the ADAMTS7/POSTN/VEGFR2 axis as a therapeutic target for PE.

stories.title: Heterogeneous knowledge distillation via architecture-aware reinforcement learning
stories.description: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers knowledge from a large teacher network to a compact student network. A central challenge in heterogeneous multi-teacher KD is balancing supervision from teachers with fundamentally different architectures—convolutional neural networks (CNNs), vision transformers (ViTs), and MLP-Mixers—whose features occupy incompatible representation spaces. Most existing methods either assume homogeneous teachers or use uniform weighting, without jointly addressing architecture-adaptive alignment and dynamic teacher weighting. We propose Heterogeneous Knowledge Distillation via Architecture-Aware Reinforcement Learning (HARKD), a framework that combines three components: (1) architecture-adaptive projectors that map heterogeneous features into compatible alignment spaces; (2) a heterogeneity-aware state representation that captures teacher performance, architectural compatibility, and branch-level alignment quality; and (3) reinforcement-learning-based optimization that dynamically weights teacher contributions across multiple student exits. The learned policy assigns depth-dependent teacher weights as the student evolves during training. Experiments on ImageNet-1K, CIFAR-100, and Tiny-ImageNet show that HARKD consistently outperforms the evaluated multi-teacher KD baselines.

stories.title: Heuriskryptes framework for identifying covert channels in neural architectures
stories.description: This paper introduces Heuriskryptes, a detection framework designed to identify AI-driven steganographic attacks within deep neural networks. The framework addresses the emerging threat of covert channels established within a model’s parameter pool. The evaluated attack vector, termed Stego-GCP, uses an orthogonal embedding to modify model weights with high stealth to leak data. To detect these channels, a specialized agent utilizes a Vision Transformer (ViT) architecture that treats the raw parameter space as an image, providing a self-attention-based mechanism that demonstrates consistent cross-architecture generalizability for efficient model auditing. The framework has been validated using a PooledCNN architecture on the Apple Disease and CIFAR-10 datasets. Results indicate that the carrier model retains a classification accuracy of 99.97%. Furthermore, the Heuriskryptes detector demonstrated high sensitivity, achieving 93.51% overall accuracy and maintaining a 90% detection rate specifically on the most challenging ambiguous, low-payload density scenarios ($$\alpha < 0.002$$). This demonstrates highly competitive performance compared to evaluated frequency-domain anomaly detection baselines. Heuriskryptes serves as a reliable detection framework for verifying model integrity in collaborative and commercial AI environments. By focusing on the structural mathematical properties of the weight spectrum rather than activation-trigger patterns, this research provides a reliable defense against the unauthorized use of neural architectures as covert communication channels.
